catalogue_requests.reason: cap.motion.joint_position.v1 takes a flat joint_positions array and requires reached and joint_positions outputs. The only command endpoint fully declared in the pinned clone is the MoveIt Servo outgoing publication of trajectory_msgs/msg/JointTrajectory: its message is a points array whose points carry positions and time_from_start, and a ROS topic publication has no controller reached result. The extension preserves the native JointTrajectory shape and reports only the publication receipt.
catalogue_requests.summary: Publish a JointTrajectory on the Servo output topic and report only publication, not execution.

notes:
BLOCKED: the pinned repository is a configuration-only ROS 2 Galactic / Gazebo Fortress / MoveIt 2 workspace for the Franka Panda. The package exposes the only command endpoint the clone fully declares: the MoveIt Servo outgoing topic /joint_trajectory_controller/joint_trajectory with type trajectory_msgs/JointTrajectory (panda_moveit_config/config/servo.yaml:15,50), as x-cap.andrejorsula.joint_trajectory.v1. A publication carries no application acknowledgement; the receipt is {published: true, confirmed: false}, so the driver makes no execution or stopped-state claim.

The acknowledged FollowJointTrajectory action that MoveIt uses (panda_moveit_config/config/moveit_controller_manager.yaml:6-9) is not exposed: the clone only names the short type FollowJointTrajectory and an exec_depend on control_msgs (panda_moveit_config/package.xml:16), so the exact control_msgs/action/FollowJointTrajectory wire type cannot be cited at this pin. The /joint_states type is likewise not declared (servo.yaml:48 only names the topic). Exposing either endpoint would fail G7 without upstream evidence.

The blocker is the safety contract. The pinned clone declares no stop, pause, controller-switch or safe-state service or action. servo.yaml:35-38 only documents Servo's own incoming_command_timeout and halt republication; it is not an acknowledged ROS stop binding. The runtime's software latch refuses further publications, but it cannot interrupt a trajectory the external joint_trajectory_controller has already accepted. The package therefore declares no safety_bindings and invents no e-stop; that is the HELPER_MISSING blocker.

Last gate output (trimmed): G1 pass Layout and isolation; G2 pass Lock; G3 pass Strict resolve; G4 pass Provenance; G5 pass Reference; G6 fail Behaviour with G6.ESTOP_FAILED: mhs.safety.estop status failed, MHS.SAFETY.SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED: the device reports that its safe state was not reached; G7 pass Native surface; G8 fail Protocol and surface with G8.CONFORMANCE MHS-Sim CL3 not achieved (CL1), failing required tests TCAP-003 and SAFE-028, G8.TEST TCAP-003 (the publication leaves resource main unchanged and returns the identical output for two distinct inputs) and G8.TEST SAFE-028 (the e-stop receipt is failed and safe_state_achieved is false); G9 skip Repository tests. MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Confirmed the block. Checked the one command binding (the absolute Servo output topic /joint_trajectory_controller/joint_trajectory and trajectory_msgs/JointTrajectory, servo.yaml:50 and 15, with ROS 2 Duration fields sec and nanosec), the seven URDF joint limits (panda.urdf:43-307, each number matches its limit line), the operator_required time bounds, every fact and the absence of a stop: the clone declares no stop, pause, controller-switch or safe-state endpoint, the FollowJointTrajectory action and /joint_states types are not declared at the pin, so the e-stop correctly reports MHS.SAFETY.SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED with the latch held and the gate fails G6.ESTOP_FAILED and G8 (SAFE-028 at R2, TCAP-003 for an unacknowledged publication). Defects: the package did not disclose that move_group.launch.py starts MoveIt Servo by default (enable_servo default true, 426-439), which publishes on the same controller topic, or that ex_ign_control.launch.py runs Gazebo with -r; and one fact turned Servo's timeout comment into a 'so ...' claim. The reviewer reworded that fact, extended the ex_ign_control fact with -r, added the launch-default fact, extended safe_state (Servo and move_group are not fenced) and added two fidelity gaps (driver.py), updated facts.md, and regenerated reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json; the stable digest of the gate report is unchanged from the author's run (RESULT.json records that run's report_digest), and the eight package cases pass. For the human reviewer: Simulation only at this pin (the ros2_control plugins are fake_components and ign_ros2_control; panda_moveit_config's README says the real robot is not yet supported). The package publishes raw JointTrajectory messages to the joint_trajectory_controller command topic, bypassing Servo's smoothing, collision checks and timeout; in a default launch Servo publishes on the same topic and move_group drives the same controller through its follow_joint_trajectory action, and the MHS latch fences neither. No stop exists in the clone: an accepted trajectory keeps executing in the free-running Gazebo after an e-stop. Unblocking needs an acknowledged stop the clone declares (for example a controller switch or a FollowJointTrajectory profile with the control_msgs type cited) and an observed joint state.
